_comment: Editorial scorecards for four delivery-pillar indicators whose underlying data is political commitments rather than machine-readable series. Each value is an editorial interpretation of published announcements (gov.uk press releases, select-committee evidence, departmental annual reports) scored as percent-of-target-milestones-hit. The shipped values are refreshed whenever the underlying departmental announcements move, typically quarterly. The adapter enforces a 90-day freshness guard so a missed refresh surfaces in /admin/health. Every entry cites its primary source URL. 2026-09-01 revisit (RUNBOOK §7: bump observed_at even when the assessment is unchanged, to record that it was reviewed): new-towns final designations (due 'later summer 2026') have not published as of 1 Sep; BICS is an application scheme opening 1 Oct 2026 rather than a live onboarding count — 81.4 held as design-complete against the 10,000-firm eligibility universe until the application window yields a take-up ratio; industrial-strategy year-one report (7 July) does not move the Q1 dashboard score; SMR site renamed Gwyndod in June, FID still 2029.

new_towns_milestones.source_label: MHCLG New Towns Draft Programme consultation (ran 23 March – 19 May 2026); consultation page still 'analysing your feedback' as of 2026-09-01, with final locations originally expected later summer 2026
new_towns_milestones.methodology: 3 of 7 shortlisted sites at planning-consent stage, 2 at outline-design, 2 at pre-scoping. Weighted by published target dates. Held at 68.0 on 2026-09-01: seven sites remain the confirmed shortlist and the consultation has closed, but final designations have not been published (the summer-2026 window has passed without a confirmation).

bics_rollout.source_label: HMT/DBT: BICS final design, 16 April 2026 (eligibility expanded to >10,000 manufacturers; applications open 1 Oct 2026; relief from Apr 2027)
bics_rollout.methodology: BICS is an eligibility/application scheme, not a live onboarding dashboard. Final design (16 April 2026) expanded the eligibility universe from ~7,000 to over 10,000 manufacturers; eligibility lists and checker followed in July–August 2026; applications open 1 October 2026; exemptions start April 2027. Held at 81.4 on 2026-09-01 as design-complete against that 10,000-firm universe (the previous '8,140 firms onboarded' interpretation is retired). Will rescore from the October application window.

industrial_strategy.source_label: DBT Industrial Strategy delivery dashboard, Q1 2026 quarterly update (published 9 April 2026); year-one report published 7 July 2026
industrial_strategy.methodology: Weighted mean of milestones tagged on-track (100), slipping (50), or missed (0) across the five published strategy pillars. Held at 74.0 on 2026-09-01: the 9 April 2026 (Q1 2026) quarterly update remains the latest scored dashboard; the 7 July year-one report restates the same 2026–27 path (BICS applications Oct 2026, relief 2027) without a new milestone-by-milestone scoreboard.

smr_programme.source_label: Great British Energy – Nuclear / Rolls-Royce SMR contract, 13 April 2026 (Wylfa, Ynys Môn — renamed Gwyndod June 2026 — confirmed as first UK SMR site)
smr_programme.methodology: Rolls-Royce SMR selected as sole vendor; Wylfa confirmed as first UK site and a site-specific design contract signed (April 2026, up to £599m from the National Wealth Fund). Site renamed Gwyndod in June 2026. Weighted against published milestones for 2030 first-steel. Held at 62.0 on 2026-09-01: the design-contract/site-confirmation milestone stands, but the major delivery milestones are unchanged — final investment decision is still expected 2029 and first-steel 2030.

release_schedule: Refreshed quarterly or on major departmental announcement.
